battle.name: 索姆河
battle.brief: 一九一六年七月一日，英法聯軍在西線索姆河打響總攻，七日砲火準備後以百萬發砲彈覆蓋德軍第二道塹壕；因砲火未能切開鐵絲網，首日英軍傷亡逾五萬。九月十五日弗萊爾—庫爾塞勒特一役，六十四噸菱形車體的馬克一號戰車首次上陣。

kit.name: 馬克 I
kit.history: 1916 年 9 月索姆河首次投入。菱形車體為了越壕。到達敵陣前，機械故障淘汰的數量不比砲火少。

countries: 一九一六年索姆河攻勢由英法聯軍在西線中段發動，參戰者很快由兩國擴展到五個帝國。英方以遠征軍總參謀部為中樞：道格拉斯·黑格自一九一五年底出任西線英軍總司令，一九一六年三月重回前線坐鎮；前線最高指揮序列依序為第一集團軍司令約翰·麥克斯韋爾、第二集團軍司令艾弗里·霍恩（九月上任）、十月接手的第四集團軍司令道格拉斯·拉斯洛森，另有指揮預備軍集團的威廉·羅伯茨。英軍序列裡除本土師外，還有加拿大第五師、紐西蘭師、澳洲師與聯合格化旅、南非第一師、印度第五師與第三師，一九一七年葡萄牙第二師亦接防同一戰區。法方由總參謀部統籌，兵權集中於福煦指揮的北方集團軍群，下轄第十軍團（貝當）、第十一軍團等，另有法軍在德軍右翼方向作牽制。德方由魯普雷希特親王領軍的集團軍群防衛，索姆河正面先後由貝洛將軍的A集團軍群與克諾貝爾斯多夫的第一集團軍守備，後由法爾肯海因接任B集團軍群指揮。兵力上，首日投入的英軍約二十餘師、法軍約十餘師，德軍在同一正面配置約五十個師，另有自東線抽調造成的空檔。
countriesEn: The Somme offensive of 1916 was launched by the Anglo-French armies in the middle of the Western Front, and the participants widened from two nations to five empires within weeks. On the British side the hub was the General Headquarters of the British Expeditionary Force: Douglas Haig had been appointed commander-in-chief on the Western Front at the end of 1915 and returned to the front in March 1916 to take charge in person. The chain of command in the line ran from First Army under Sir John Maxwell, to Second Army under Sir Arthur Horne, who took over in September, to Fourth Army under Sir Douglas Rawlinson, who assumed command in October, while Lieutenant-General Sir William Roberts commanded the Reserve Army massed for the offensive. The British order of battle held not only home units but the Canadian 5th Division, the New Zealand Division, the Australian Division and its combined corps, the South African 1st Division, and the Indian 5th and 3rd Divisions; in 1917 the Portuguese 2nd Division took over a sector of the same battlefield. The French side was coordinated by the General Headquarters, with the actual troops concentrated in the Groupe d'armees du Nord under Foch, comprising the Tenth Army under Petain, the Eleventh Army and others, while French forces mounted a diversion against the German right flank. Germany was defended by an army group under Crown Prince Rupprecht of Bavaria; the Somme front was held in turn by Army Group A under von Below and the First Army under von Knobelsdorff, and Falkenhayn later took over Army Group B. In men, the British committed upwards of twenty divisions and the French more than ten on the opening day, against roughly fifty German divisions on the same front, a situation worsened by the transfer of German troops from the west to the east.
people: 英方最具影響力的是黑格：他視索姆河為一次可望扭轉西線僵局的總攻，主張以七日砲火準備換取縱深推進，十月把戰線北翼的指揮交給霍恩，並在第四集團軍引入拉斯洛森與坦克協同的新作法；參謀長亨利·霍蘭與炮兵參謀主管制訂了極密集的射表。第一集團軍司令麥克斯韋爾負責首日攻勢，第四集團軍司令拉斯洛森在瓦朗庫爾丘一役中以戰車掩護步兵的做法最為成熟。法方實際統兵的是福煦與貝當，貝當在十月守住了德軍反攻最猛烈的地段。戰車這條線上的關鍵人物是英國軍用船舶委員會主席戴維·羅伯茨、海軍大臣溫斯頓·丘吉爾，以及陸軍作戰局主任斯溫頓中將；設計者則是福斯特公司的威廉·特里頓與軍械委員會的戈登·威爾森中校，後者在一九一四年底提出以「陸上戰艦」跨越壕溝的構思，該構思到一九一六年八月才以馬克一號問世。德方主導者是貝洛、克諾貝爾斯多夫與法爾肯海因，魯登道夫則在同年秋把重心轉回東線。
peopleEn: The most influential man on the British side was Haig. He treated the Somme as a general offensive that might break the stalemate on the western front, argued for a seven-day bombardment in exchange for a deep advance, handed command of the northern flank to Horne in October, and introduced Rawlinson and the new practice of tank-supported infantry to Fourth Army. The chief of staff Henry Horne and the artillery staff worked out an extremely dense fire plan. Sir John Maxwell, commanding First Army, directed the opening attack, and Rawlinson at Fourth Army produced the most mature version of tank-supported assault at Warlencourt. On the French side actual command lay with Foch and Petain, and Petain held the most heavily pressed sector against the German counter-offensive in October. On the tank side the key figures were David Roberts, chairman of the Landships Committee, Winston Churchill as First Lord of the Admiralty, and Major-General Sir Ernest Swinton, director of military operations. The designers were William Tritton of William Foster and Company and Lieutenant-Colonel Walter Gordon Wilson of the Landships Committee, who had proposed in late 1914 a land vessel able to cross trenches; that idea only became the Mark I in August 1916. On the German side the leading figures were von Below, von Knobelsdorff and Falkenhayn, while Ludendorff shifted his centre of gravity back to the east in the autumn of the same year.
kits: 馬克一號戰車是英軍機械化部隊的試作裝備：由肯特郡利思希思的國營兵工廠、利茲與克萊頓的F.M.S.廠等處生產，各型號合計至一九一八年約三千五百輛。車體為菱形，首要目的就是跨越寬約四至六公尺的戰壕與破壞帶；全車長約八點四五公尺、寬約二點一一公尺、高約二點四四公尺，噸位約二十八至三十二噸，乘員八人，裝甲厚約六至八毫米。動力為兩具四汽缸汽油機，平地最高時速約六點四公里，崎嶇泥濘路面僅約二點四公里，單次加滿燃料可行約四十公里。武器是車首一門六磅（五十七毫米）快砲，兩側突出部各置一挺維克斯式三〇三機槍。它在索姆河體系中的位置很清楚：九月十五日弗萊爾—庫爾塞勒特一役投入十一輛，結果多數陷在泥濘、被砲火擊毀或因機械故障拋錨，到十六日只剩數輛。與它並存的大宗舊裝備仍是主力：英軍李—恩菲爾德步槍、維克斯機槍、十八磅野戰砲、六吋與九吋榴彈砲、戰壕迫擊砲與火焰噴射器；德軍則有毛瑟九八式步槍、MG 08重機槍、七七與十點五厘米野戰砲、一五厘米重榴彈砲及四二厘米戰壕臼砲。德軍在整場索姆河裡沒有可用的戰車對手，其A7V要到一九一七年三月才首次上陣。
kitsEn: The Mark I tank was the experimental equipment of the British mechanised arm: it was produced at the state arsenal at Little Heath in Kent, at Leeds and Clayton by the F.M.S. works and elsewhere, and about three thousand five hundred of all marks had been built by 1918. The hull was a rhomboid, and its first purpose was to cross trenches and the shattered ground band some four to six metres wide. The vehicle was about 8.45 metres long, 2.11 metres wide and 2.44 metres high, weighed roughly twenty-eight to thirty-two tons, carried a crew of eight and had armour some six to eight millimetres thick. Power came from two four-cylinder petrol engines, giving about 6.4 kilometres per hour on the flat and only about 2.4 on rough muddy ground, with a range of around forty kilometres on one filling of fuel. Its armament was one 6-pounder (57mm) quick-firing gun in the front of the hull and one Vickers .303 machine gun in each of the side sponsons. Its place in the Somme system was plain: eleven vehicles were committed in the Battle of Flers-Courcelette on 15 September, and most of them either bogged down, were destroyed by shellfire or broke down mechanically, leaving only a few still running on the sixteenth. The bulk of the equipment on the battlefield remained older: the Lee-Enfield rifle, the Vickers machine gun, the 18-pounder field gun, 6-inch and 9-inch howitzers, trench mortars and flamethrowers on the British side; on the German side the Gewehr 98, the MG 08 heavy machine gun, 7.7cm and 10.5cm field guns, the 15cm heavy howitzer and the 42cm trench mortar. Germany had no usable tank counterpart anywhere in the Somme campaign; its A7V did not see action until March 1917.
tactics: 一九一六年七月一日早上七時三十分為「零時」，英軍各師在縱深集結完畢後，步兵按營縱隊由北向南逐段躍進：第一批部隊用白粉彈、手榴彈與刺刀在鐵絲網上撕出缺口，第二批用剪鉗與炸藥包在缺口上架設便橋，第三批才向前佔領敵壕。整條攻擊正面自阿斯克河到塞雷約五十公里，英軍重壓約四十公里，而德軍在前線佈了三至四道鐵絲網帶，英方工程部門估計光為剪網便需約一百六十萬發小口徑切割彈與約十萬枚炸藥包，實際成功切開的比例仍極低。砲火準備自六月二十四日起持續七日，總量以百萬計，卻多數只是打成彈坑與地雷爆炸，未能有效壓制機槍巢。步兵裝備負荷普遍在六十公斤以上，越過四至六公尺的破壞帶已耗盡體力，許多次連一線都未到便被機槍與手榴彈消滅。九月十五日戰車加入攻勢，十一輛馬克一號在三十分鐘內連續越壕，因無人掩護而幾乎全毀；十月第四集團軍改為讓戰車先行越壕、步兵在掩體後跟進。德軍一至四日的反攻以突擊兵滲透配合集中砲火進行，雙方在塹壕與坑道之間反覆拉鋸，後方則靠臨時鐵路與卡車把每日數百噸的砲彈、糧秣與飲水送上去。
tacticsEn: At 07:30 on 1 July 1916 was zero hour. After assembling in depth the British divisions advanced in battalion columns, leapfrogging from north to south: the first wave tore gaps in the wire with white phosphorus, grenades and bayonets, the second bridged the gaps with clippers and explosive charges, and only the third moved up to storm the German trench. The whole attacking front ran some fifty kilometres from the Ancre to Serre, of which the British pressed about forty, while the Germans had three to four belts of barbed wire in front of the front line. British engineers reckoned that cutting the wire alone required something like 1.6 million rounds of small-calibre cutting shell and about 100,000 explosive charges, and in practice only a very small fraction of the wire was opened. The bombardment ran for seven days from 24 June and involved a million rounds, but most of it merely cratered the ground and set off buried mines without silencing the machine-gun posts. The infantryman carried more than sixty kilograms of equipment, and crossing a band four to six metres deep already exhausted him; many were destroyed by machine gun and grenade before reaching the German wire. Tanks joined the attack on 15 September, eleven Mark Is crossing in succession inside half an hour, and were almost all lost for want of infantry cover; in October Fourth Army changed the drill so that the tanks went over first and the infantry followed under cover. The German counter-offensive of 1 to 4 October was fought with stormtrooper infiltration supported by concentrated artillery, both sides traded attacks across trenches and dugouts, and at the rear temporary railway lines and lorries carried several hundred tonnes of shells, rations and water forward each day.
data: 索姆河攻勢自一九一六年七月一日打到十一月十八日，前後一百四十一日。正面自北面的阿斯克河到南面的塞雷，長約五十公里，實際重點攻擊段約四十公里。砲火準備七日發彈約一百五十萬發，另有前一周的間歇砲擊。首日英軍傷亡逾五萬七千人，其中官方記錄陣亡約一萬九千餘人；紐芬蘭第一步兵團在博蒙哈梅爾一役一日之內傷亡逾七百人；一九一六年七月十八日其後被英方視為整場戰爭中最黑暗的一日。英軍在戰役結尾時把德軍戰線向後推約八至十公里，最深處一度達十九公里，德軍在若干地段向後撤退一至二公里以鞏固新陣地。雙方總傷亡以百萬計：英軍約四十二萬、法軍約二十萬、德軍約五十萬以上，各方統計口徑不一，諸說並存。馬克一號的諸項數字是：全車長八點四五公尺、寬二點一一公尺、高二點四四公尺、重約二十八至三十二噸、乘員八人、平地時速約六點四公里、崎嶇路面約二點四公里、單次續航約四十公里；九月十五日一次出動十一輛，數日內損失十輛。
dataEn: The Somme offensive ran from 1 July to 18 November 1916, a span of one hundred and forty-one days. The front extended some fifty kilometres from the Ancre in the north to Serre in the south, with about forty kilometres receiving the weight of the main effort. The seven days of bombardment fired roughly one and a half million shells, in addition to the intermittent bombardment of the preceding week. British casualties on the first day exceeded fifty-seven thousand, of whom the official count gives about nineteen thousand two hundred dead; the Newfoundland Regiment lost more than seven hundred men in a single day at Beaumont-Hamel, and 18 July 1916 was afterwards regarded by the British as the blackest day of the whole battle. By the end of the campaign the British had pushed the German line back some eight to ten kilometres, at one point as much as nineteen kilometres, while the Germans withdrew one or two kilometres in places to consolidate new positions. Total casualties ran to over a million: about four hundred and twenty thousand British, about two hundred thousand French and more than five hundred thousand German, though the counting differs from source to source and the figures are much disputed. The Mark I figures are these: 8.45 metres long, 2.11 metres wide, 2.44 metres high, weighing roughly twenty-eight to thirty-two tons, crew of eight, 6.4 kilometres per hour on the flat and 2.4 on rough ground, a range of some forty kilometres on one filling of fuel; eleven went into action on 15 September and ten were lost within days.
cause: 索姆河的開打，是一九一六年西線僵持下的產物。一九一五年德軍在東線得利後退守興登堡防線，放棄在西線求戰的餘地；凡爾登一役雖令德軍付出慘重代價，卻也顯示純粹的進攻消耗太大，雙方都需要換一種方式打破平衡。直接背景是英國的砲彈短缺危機：一九一五年的軍需調查揭發了產能與分配上的問題，兵工廠隨後大規模擴充，到一九一六年夏已有足夠砲彈支撐七日以上的密集砲火，攻勢時機因此成熟。戰略上，俄軍布魯西洛夫在六月的東線攻勢牽制了大量德軍，魯登道夫被迫把兵員往東移；英法聯軍五月在巴黎的會議上決定發動大規模協同攻勢，黑格選中索姆河，一是該段德軍陣地最堅固，二是阿爾貝至亞眠的鐵路可以平行推進、能解決補給難題。計畫原定八月底，因砲彈不足順延到七月一日。黑格相信德軍已無力再承受一次大規模衝擊，加上截獲文件顯示德軍第二線兵力單薄，遂以七日砲擊加全線同時進攻取代逐步滲透。
causeEn: The Somme was the product of the stalemate on the western front in 1916. After its successes in the east in 1915 Germany withdrew to the Hindenburg Line and gave up any ambition of seeking a decision in the west. Verdun had cost Germany dearly and had shown that sheer attack consumed both sides faster than it decided anything, so both wanted a different way to break the balance. The immediate background was the British shell shortage: the 1915 munitions inquiry exposed problems of production and distribution, the arsenals were then expanded on a large scale, and by the summer of 1916 there were enough shells for a bombardment of more than seven days, which made the moment ripe. Strategically, Brusilov's Russian offensive in June tied down large German forces and Ludendorff was obliged to move men eastward. The Entente conference at Paris in May decided on a large coordinated offensive, and Haig chose the Somme because that stretch of German line was the strongest and because the railway from Albert to Amiens could be pushed forward alongside the advance, solving the problem of supply. The plan had originally been set for late August and was postponed to 1 July for want of shells. Haig believed Germany could not absorb another mass assault, and captured documents suggested the German second line was thinly held, so he substituted a seven-day bombardment and a simultaneous attack along the whole front for step-by-step infiltration.
impact: 索姆河最重要的技術後果，是戰車由奇觀變成兵種。第一次投入即暴露諸多毛病：越壕能力雖成，機動力、可靠性與防砲力都不足，而且完全缺乏步兵與炮兵的配合規範，於是改良接連而來，車體加高加寬、引擎馬力提升，出現馬克二、三、四型，一九一七年康布雷一役以數百輛集群使用，裝甲車的戰術地位由此確立。另一個後果是突擊兵制度：德軍在十月反攻中以小單位滲透配合輕重武器，收回部分失地，英軍亦在十一月瓦朗庫爾丘一役中建立戰車與步兵的協同準則；「不做正面強攻」的思路，於一九一七至一九一八年間成為各國主流。制度上，德軍在失利後把防線改成更深的已完成塹壕，並首次為 MG 08 陣位構築混凝土堡壘；英軍則因索姆河經驗而擴大炮兵編制、更新射表、改進戰壕深度與防空。政治與輿論上，一九一六年成為英國的政治危機之年，首相更替，輿論開始質疑西線的傷亡模式，一九一七年的戰爭失職委員會報告即是此種壓力的產物；同年秋倫敦的「召回死者」遊行、戰爭疲勞與反戰言論，都把索姆河塑造成「徒勞」的代名詞。德軍方面，一九一六年秋的索姆河消耗加速了其內部的政治危機，並促使魯登道夫把重心放在無限制潛艇戰上。
impactEn: The chief technical consequence of the Somme was the tank's passage from curiosity to arm. Its first use exposed every weakness: the ability to cross trenches worked, but mobility, reliability and protection against shellfire were all inadequate, and there was no doctrine at all for the coordination of tanks with infantry and artillery. Improvement followed quickly, with taller and wider hulls and more powerful engines giving rise to the Mark II, III and IV, and at Cambrai in 1917 several hundred were used in mass, which fixed the tactical position of the armoured vehicle. A second consequence was the stormtrooper system: the German counter-offensive in October used small-unit infiltration with combined light and heavy weapons to recover lost ground, and the British established their own rules for tank and infantry cooperation at Warlencourt in November. The idea of refusing frontal mass assault became mainstream between 1917 and 1918. Institutionally, the Germans after their reverse turned the line into a deeper completed trench system and built concrete gun emplacements for their MG 08 positions for the first time; the British, taking the lesson of the Somme, expanded their artillery establishment, revised their fire tables and improved the depth of their trenches and their anti-aircraft work. In politics and opinion, 1916 became the year of the British political crisis, with a change of prime minister and open questioning of the casualty pattern in the west; the report of the committee on the misconduct of the war in 1917 grew out of that pressure. The autumn procession of the 'Recalled Dead' in London, war weariness and the growth of anti-war argument all fixed the Somme in memory as the emblem of futility. On the German side the consumption of the autumn of 1916 quickened the internal political crisis and pushed Ludendorff toward unrestricted submarine warfare.

resultEn: The Somme ended in a costly and limited victory. The Anglo-French armies finally took some fifty square kilometres of ground, captured villages such as Fricourt and Beaumont-Hamel and the heights above Albert, and stormed the Butte de Warlencourt on 14 November, but the main German defensive line remained intact on most of the front; the Allied armies won no operational breakthrough, and the line moved back on average by only eight to ten kilometres. The cost was heavy: more than a million casualties in all, roughly four hundred and twenty thousand British, two hundred thousand French and over half a million German. The British army was so exhausted by the Somme that it did not regain the capacity for a major offensive until 1917. On 18 November 1916 the Allied attack was reduced to the capture of limited objectives and the campaign effectively ended, and the western front returned once more to stalemate. The technical and tactical harvest, however, was real: the tank became a permanent arm of the British army, fire tables and methods of coordination between artillery and infantry were standardised, infiltration tactics were born on both sides, and the scale of the sapper, mining and underground war grew greatly. The Somme ended the stalemate of the war's first year without ending the war itself. It fixed the modern form of war, in which the outcome is decided by industrial output, materiel and endurance, and from then on the contest in the west ran along two lines: the speed of production and the pace of tactical innovation.
